description: Illustrative minimal governance-plurality registry — one axis proven by a repeated field on the governed thing, one proven by a collection of records each referencing the one thing, and one field that must stay singular. The canonical registry carries the full axis set.

measurement.note: Every schema parsed in full and walked to any depth, so a nested repeated field is not mistaken for a missing one.

axes.name: Multi-jurisdiction
axes.question: Can one evidence record hold every jurisdiction whose law applied to the decision at the same moment?

axes.name: Multi-auditor
axes.question: Can several auditors independently stand on one sealed record, each reaching their own conclusion?

proof.attaches_to: the bundle that carries the sealed record

axes.name: Tenant identity — singular by design
axes.question: Should a tenant-scoped record carry several tenant ids at once? No, and the reason is recorded here.

proof.reason: Isolation is a predicate over exactly one tenant. A predicate over a set is not an isolation boundary, so making this field repeated would turn a tenancy control into an unaudited cross-tenant read.

declared_arity_caps.reason: The set is closed by the canon at ten members, so the cap encodes an enumeration rather than a limit on how many may apply at once.
